Qwen3.5 (qwen3_5, transformers 5.8) builds an explicit float attention mask even for text-only inputs (to support image-token regions). Torch mem-efficient SDPA backward then allocates a (heads, T, T) fp32 grad-bias buffer — 9.77 GiB at T=12.8k on Qwen3.5-4B — and flash SDP rejects head_dim 256. **Why:** the mask is plain causal for text-only batches, so materializing it is pure waste.

**How to apply:** use `sdft/patches.py` (`attn_implementation: sdpa_textonly` in the config) which registers an AttentionInterface entry passing `is_causal=query_len>1` and mask=None. Text-only batches ONLY — wrong for image inputs. A from-scratch, browser-based recreation of Pokémon FireRed featuring **all 151
Gen-1 Pokémon** with their real FireRed/LeafGreen battle sprites, real base
stats, level-up learnsets, and full evolution chains.

**Fan project for personal/educational use.** Pokémon is © Nintendo / Game
Freak / Creatures Inc. Sprite art and species data are fetched from the
community-run [PokeAPI](https://pokeapi.co/). Don't distribute or monetize.

## Play

Open `index.html` in any modern browser. That's it — no build step, no server.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Arrows / WASD | Move |
| Z / Space | A — confirm, talk, read signs, fish at water |
| X / Esc | B — cancel |
| Enter / M | Start menu — Pokédex, party, bag, save |

## What's in the game

- **Overworld**: Pallet Town, Route 1, Viridian City (Center + Mart), Route 2,
  Viridian Forest, Mt. Moon Foot Cave, Pewter City and Gym — tile-based maps
  with warps, NPCs, signs, and trainer line-of-sight.
- **Story**: Get a starter from Prof. Oak, beat your rival, cross the forest,
  defeat Brock for the Boulder Badge.
- **Battles**: Gen-3 mechanics — damage formula, type chart (no Fairy, it's
  2004), the type-based physical/special split, STAB, crits, stat stages,
  accuracy/evasion, status conditions (PSN/BRN/PAR/SLP/FRZ), confusion,
  Leech Seed, Reflect/Light Screen, multi-hit moves, fixed-damage and OHKO
  moves, Metronome, Transform, Struggle, priority, and the real Gen-3
  catch-rate formula.
- **Progression**: exp with the correct growth curves, level-up move learning
  (with move-forgetting), level evolutions, stone evolutions (stones sold at
  the Viridian Mart), PC box storage, money, a working Pokédex.
- **All 151 obtainable, single-player**: every base form spawns somewhere
  (grass, cave, or fishing with the Old Rod from the boy on Route 1); trade
  evolutions are converted to level-up at Lv. 37; legendaries are ultra-rare
  deep-cave encounters; Mew haunts Viridian Forest (1/1000).
- **Audio**: GB-style synth — chiptune loops, battle/heal/catch/evolve jingles.

## Development

```
npm install            # puppeteer-core (testing only)
npm run fetch-data     # re-download data + sprites from PokeAPI
npm run validate       # data integrity + all-151-obtainable proof
npm test               # headless browser playthrough of the opening
```

Everything except the Pokémon sprites (PNGs in `assets/sprites/`) is generated
in code: tiles, character sprites, the 5×7 bitmap font, UI chrome, and music
are all drawn/synthesized at boot.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `js/typechart.js` | Gen-3 type chart + physical/special-by-type rule |
| `js/pokemon.js`   | Stats math, exp curves, evolution, items |
| `js/maps.js`      | World maps (char grids), NPCs, trainers, encounter tables |
| `js/battle.js`    | Battle engine, move-effect interpreter, AI, catching |
| `js/overworld.js` | Movement, camera, warps, encounters, story scripts |
| `js/ui.js`        | Dialog/menus/party/bag/Pokédex widgets |
| `js/gfx.js`       | Procedural tileset, character sprites, bitmap font |
| `js/audio.js`     | WebAudio square-wave synth |
| `js/game.js`      | Boot, title, save/load (localStorage), main loop |

## KILLHOUSE — your tactical CQB shooter is live

**Play it now at http://localhost:5173** (the dev server is running in the background). Click to capture the mouse and breach.

First, honest framing: true Siege-level photorealism comes from Unreal Engine 5, scanned assets, and art teams — no one can generate that in code alone. What I built instead is a complete, playable tactical FPS in Three.js with the *mechanics and feel* of a Siege-style CQB round, and visuals pushed as far as procedural assets allow (PBR materials, real-time shadows, ACES filmic tone mapping, fog, dust motes in the skylight shaft).

**The game:** You breach a killhouse — a 40×30m kill-zone of rooms, corridors, crates, and chest-high cover — and clear 8 patrolling hostiles. They have a 120° vision cone with real line-of-sight raycasts, a human reaction delay, burst fire with distance-based accuracy, and they investigate gunshots and hunt your last known position. Die and you're K.I.A. — no respawns mid-round. Clearing the building shows your kills, accuracy, and time.

**Gunplay:** Full-auto 700 RPM rifle with aim-down-sights (FOV zoom + sight alignment), recoil with recovery, hip-fire spread vs. ADS precision, movement penalty on accuracy, 30-round mags with a 2.2s reload animation, muzzle flash lighting, tracers, impact particles and scorch marks, headshots (1-tap) vs. body shots (3-tap), and hit/kill markers. All sound — gunshots, distant enemy fire panned by direction, footsteps, reloads, ricochets — is synthesized live in WebAudio, so there are zero asset files.

**Controls:** WASD move, Shift sprint, C/Ctrl crouch, Q/E lean (peeks your camera around cover, just like Siege), RMB aim, R reload.

The code is organized for you to extend: `src/world.js` (map, lighting, enemy spawn/patrol definitions), `src/enemy.js` (AI state machine), `src/weapon.js` (gun handling — add weapons by tweaking the stats at the top), `src/main.js` (player controller, combat, HUD), `src/audio.js`. ## What I built

A self-evolving trading strategy system in [D:\project-4](README.md) with four modules:

- **[main.py](main.py)** — CLI. `--dry-run` tests the backtester offline; `--generations N` runs the evolution loop; `--reset` clears memory.
- **[data.py](data.py)** — loads real OHLCV from `data/<TICKER>.csv` if present, otherwise generates synthetic regime-switching (bull/bear/sideways) price data so it runs with no network access.
- **[backtester.py](backtester.py)** — executes generated strategy code in a subprocess with a 30s timeout, enforces no-lookahead (today's signal earns tomorrow's return), charges 10 bps transaction costs, and computes Sharpe, drawdown, win rate, trades, and a buy-and-hold benchmark.
- **[evolver.py](evolver.py)** — the Claude loop (Opus 4.8, adaptive thinking, streaming). Each generation it prompts with the top-3 strategies (full code + metrics) and recent failures (error tracebacks + post-mortems), gets back a hypothesis and a `generate_signals(df)` function, backtests it on train and held-out test splits, then asks Claude for a 2–3 sentence post-mortem. Everything persists to `history.json`, so learning carries across generations *and* across runs.

**How it learns from failures:** failures come in three flavors and all feed back into the prompt — crashes (full traceback shown), overfitting (fitness explicitly penalizes train-Sharpe ≫ test-Sharpe), and degenerate strategies (near-zero trading scores −1). The model writes its own post-mortem after every attempt, which becomes the institutional memory future generations read.

Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) of an open student model (default
`Qwen/Qwen3-8B`) on the agentic coding traces in
[`armand0e/qwen3.7-max-pi-traces`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/armand0e/qwen3.7-max-pi-traces),
**without** destructive cross-entropy SFT.

## Why not plain SFT?

Cross-entropy on teacher-written tokens is *off-policy*: it forces probability
mass onto sequences the student would never produce itself, dragging the whole
distribution sideways and causing catastrophic forgetting ("destructive SFT").
Classic on-policy distillation (GKD / on-policy KD) fixes this by scoring the
student's *own* rollouts against the teacher's per-token distribution — but the
trace author, `qwen/qwen3.7-max`, is an API model with no logit access.

**SDFT closes the gap by making the model its own teacher:**

| | input | role |
|---|---|---|
| **student** `π_θ( · \| context)` | the conversation so far | trainable, generates rollouts |
| **teacher** `π_0( · \| context + expert turn in-context)` | same context **plus** the qwen3.7-max turn injected as an `<expert_reference>` block | frozen base weights |

Conditioning the frozen base on the demonstration steers its next-token
distribution toward the expert's behavior *while staying inside the base
model's own distribution*. Each training step:

1. Sample conversation contexts (one example per assistant turn in a trace).
2. The **student rolls out its own response** (sampling, current weights).
3. The teacher scores every rollout token: full-vocab logits over the same
   tokens, conditioned on the reference-augmented prompt.
4. Minimize exact per-token **reverse KL(student ‖ teacher)** — mode-seeking,
   the standard on-policy distillation loss. Forward KL and generalized JSD
   are also available (`distill.kind`).

With LoRA the teacher is **free**: it is the identical network with the
adapter disabled (`model.disable_adapter()`), so only one copy of the weights
lives on the GPU. With full fine-tuning a second frozen copy is loaded
automatically.

`distill.lambda_on_policy < 1.0` mixes in a fraction of steps scored on the
expert's *own* tokens (rendered through the chat template) — still KL against
the teacher distribution, never plain cross-entropy, mirroring GKD's
λ-mixture.

## Layout

```
sdft/
  trace_parser.py   teich JSONL events -> normalized OpenAI-style messages
  data.py           student prompt / teacher prompt / expert-target rendering
  rollout.py        batched left-padded sampling from the current student
  distill.py        exact chunked fp32 token-level KL / JSD
scripts/
  prepare_data.py   download traces from the Hub, flatten to per-turn examples
  inspect_data.py   preview rendered prompts for one example
  train_sdft.py     the on-policy SDFT training loop
configs/
  sdft.yaml         all hyperparameters
  tools.json        pi tool schemas (read / bash / edit / write) passed to the
                    chat template so rollouts emit well-formed tool calls
```

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

# 1. Flatten traces into per-turn examples (data/examples.jsonl)
python scripts/prepare_data.py --repo armand0e/qwen3.7-max-pi-traces --out data/examples.jsonl

# 2. Sanity-check what the trainer will see
python scripts/inspect_data.py --index 0                      # raw messages
python scripts/inspect_data.py --index 0 --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B  # rendered prompts

# 3. Train
python scripts/train_sdft.py --config configs/sdft.yaml
```

Checkpoints (LoRA adapter + tokenizer) land in `outputs/sdft-qwen3-8b/step-*`
and `.../final`. Load with `peft.PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, adapter_path)`
or merge with `merge_and_unload()`.
